open_questions: Grazing impact parameter 0.9628 and long duration (ratio 1.51) limit radius precision and make the achromatic transit flat-bottom verification difficult; high-resolution spectroscopy/RVs are still needed to exclude a grazing stellar companion mass near the planet radius
Only 3 transits with SNR 13.34 were found and expected_share 0.1784 vs observed share 0.403 (p_chance 0.005676); additional transits are required to confirm period and refine impact parameter
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a consistent 4058 ppm flat-bottom dip every 14 days around a K dwarf at 94 light-years, with no odd-even change, no second eclipse and no neighbour able to mimic it. The dip is too small for a star (3.3 Earth radii) and the long, grazing geometry explains why the duration is longer than central. With only three transits seen so far the size and orbit still need radial-velocity confirmation, but a planet is the best explanation.

reasons.why: Planet-sized dip: 3.275 Rearth with rp/rstar 0.06381, well below the giant-planet/star limit. Large star density penalty (fit_log_density_ratio -2.508, penalty 52.84) is owed to the long duration and is absorbed by the grazing impact parameter.
Duration up to 1.5x central is allowed for off-centre/grazing geometry; long duration and b=0.9628 indicate an almost fully grazing transit, not a stellar eclipse requiring extra density discrepancy.
reasons.value: observed 4 h vs central 2.65 h, ratio 1.509; fit_b 0.9628, t14_h 7.2

reasons.why: No V shape, no significant odd/even difference, no secondary dip at any phase. Explains away both eclipsing-binary signatures despite the xgboost planet_rank 0.05 low score, which is driven by the few transits and grazing geometry.
reasons.value: v_sigma 1.504, odd_even diff_sigma 0.8452 (odd 3842 vs even 4380 ppm), secondary snr 2.328 vs best_brightening_snr 2.598

reasons.why: Depths are consistent within one sector, no evidence for a neighbour dilution. Flat bottom (v_sigma <3) favours planet over a small star grazing eclipse, which would show a hotter shape and stronger variability.
reasons.value: 3 transits mean 4028 ppm (p_consistent 0.267), sectors p_constant 1, neighbours plausible_within_1px 0, could_cause_within_1px 0

reasons.why: No measured rotation period to associate with, and out-of-transit variability is low (ratio 0.1087, variability_chi2_dof 1.32), ruling out spot-driven false positives as the cause of the 14-d signal.
